title: Croydon Emergency Help Points
summary: 24/7 emergency hospitals, urgent treatment centres, and local hazards across Croydon borough.
content:
For immediate life-threatening medical emergencies, always dial 999 first.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals with A&E
- Croydon University Hospital: 530 London Road, Thornton Heath, CR7 7YE. From West Croydon station: ~15 min walk north along London Road (A235), or take bus 60, 64, 109, 198, or 250 directly to the hospital entrance.
- Major Trauma Centre: St George's Hospital, Blackshaw Road, Tooting, SW17 0QT (serving South West London and Surrey). From East Croydon station: train to Balham or Clapham Junction, then Northern line to Tooting Broadway, followed by a ~10 min walk along Cranmer Terrace.

2. Urgent Treatment Centres (Walk-In)
- Croydon Urgent Treatment Centre: 530 London Road, CR7 7YE (collocated at Croydon University Hospital). Open 24/7.
- Purley Urgent Treatment Centre: Purley War Memorial Hospital, 856 Brighton Road, Purley, CR8 2YL. From Purley station: ~5 min walk south along Brighton Road (A235).

3. Local Area Hazard Notes
- River Wandle: headwater springs and drainage routes around Waddon Ponds can flood low-lying ground during extended rainfall.
- Surface-Water Flooding: the dry chalk valley across Coulsdon, Kenley, and Purley Cross is prone to intense surface runoff and groundwater flooding.

4. Essential Supplies During Outages
Pharmacies and large supermarkets along North End (Croydon town centre), George Street, London Road, and Brighton Road (Purley) can supply drinking water, basic first-aid supplies, and over-the-counter medicines.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
